steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up basic HTML structure
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and add a basic HTML structure with two sections that we'll transition between.
steps.hint: Start by creating a CSS file and adding the basic HTML structure with two sections.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Basic HTML structure with two sections */
/* This is the foundation for view transitions */
steps.seedCode: /* Create a CSS file and add basic HTML structure with two sections */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file is created with a basic HTML structure containing two sections.
successCriteria: CSS file exists with basic HTML structure containing two sections.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the foundation for view transitions with two sections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have two sections in your HTML structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a CSS file with basic HTML structure containing two sections.

steps.title: Add initial styling for the two view sections
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules to style the two sections with different background colors, positioning, and basic layout.
steps.hint: Use the section selectors to set background-color, position, width, height, and other layout properties.
steps.seedCode:
/* Create a CSS file and add basic HTML structure with two sections */

/* Add your CSS rules here to style the two sections */
steps.expectedOutcome: Two distinct sections with different background colors and positioning are styled, ready for transition demonstration.
successCriteria: Two sections are styled with different background colors, positioning properties, and basic layout rules.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully styled both sections with distinct visual styles.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure both sections have different background colors and proper positioning.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sections don't have the required styling. Check that you've added CSS rules for both sections with different background colors and positioning.

steps.title: Add the view-transition-name property to the first section
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property `view-transition-name` with the value 'main-content' to the first section's selector.
steps.hint: Look for the selector for the first section in your CSS and add `view-transition-name: 'main-content';` as a new rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first section will be identified with the name 'main-content' for view transitions.
successCriteria: The CSS selector for the first section includes `view-transition-name: 'main-content';`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully named the first section for view transitions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added `view-transition-name: 'main-content';` to the correct selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for the first section is missing or incorrect. Ensure it includes `view-transition-name: 'main-content';`.

steps.title: Add the view-transition-name property to the second section
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property `view-transition-name: 'sidebar';` to the second section to create a second named transition element.
steps.hint: Target the second section selector and add the property with the value 'sidebar' in quotes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second section will have a view-transition-name property set to 'sidebar', making it a named transition element alongside the first section.
successCriteria: The second section selector includes the property `view-transition-name: 'sidebar';`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a view-transition-name to the second section, creating two named elements for transitions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the property is correctly spelled and the value is 'sidebar' in quotes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second section doesn't have the required view-transition-name property. Check the selector and property syntax.

steps.title: Add basic view transition animation with view-transition-group
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the ::view-transition-group pseudo-element to define a basic animation duration and easing function.
steps.hint: Use the ::view-transition-group pseudo-element selector and set the animation-duration and animation-timing-function properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The view transition between the two sections will have a smooth 0.5-second animation with easing.
successCriteria: A CSS rule for ::view-transition-group is added with animation-duration and animation-timing-function properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the animation properties for the view transition group, which will create a smooth transition between the two sections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some animation properties, but make sure to include both animation-duration and animation-timing-function for the ::view-transition-group pseudo-element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for ::view-transition-group with animation properties is missing. Add a rule targeting ::view-transition-group with animation-duration and animation-timing-function.

steps.title: Customize the transition duration
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to set the view transition duration to 1 second, making the animation slower and more visible.
steps.hint: Use the view-transition-duration property with a value of 1s.
steps.expectedOutcome: The view transition animation will now take 1 second to complete, making it noticeably slower.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a view-transition-duration property set to 1s.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set the view transition duration to 1 second. This makes the animation slower and more visible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property name and value. Try using 'view-transition-duration: 1s;'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem to be the correct way to set the view transition duration. The property should be 'view-transition-duration' with a value of '1s'.

steps.title: Add easing function to the transition
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to apply an easing function to your view transition using the view-transition-timing-function property.
steps.hint: Use the property view-transition-timing-function with a value like ease-in-out to make the animation smoother.
steps.expectedOutcome: The view transition will have a smooth acceleration and deceleration effect.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a view-transition-timing-function property with a value like ease-in-out.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added an easing function to make the transition smoother.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the correct property name: view-transition-timing-function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the property name and value. It should be view-transition-timing-function with a value like ease-in-out.

steps.title: Style the ::view-transition pseudo-element
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style the ::view-transition pseudo-element by setting its background color to a light gray (e.g., #f0f0f0).
steps.hint: Use the ::view-transition pseudo-element selector and set the background-color property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The overall transition container will have a light gray background during view transitions.
successCriteria: A ::view-transition rule with background-color property is added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've styled the transition container, giving it a distinct background during animations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the ::view-transition selector and setting a background-color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't match the expected styling for the transition container. Review the ::view-transition pseudo-element.

steps.title: Style individual transition elements with ::view-transition-group
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style the ::view-transition-group pseudo-element for the 'main-content' view transition name with a background color of lightblue.
steps.hint: Use the ::view-transition-group pseudo-element with the specific view transition name in parentheses to target it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The 'main-content' transition group will have a light blue background during the view transition.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a ::view-transition-group(main-content) rule with background-color: lightblue;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully targeted the 'main-content' transition group with custom styling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct selector syntax and property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for styling the 'main-content' transition group is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add crossfade effect between the two sections
steps.instruction: Add opacity transitions to the ::view-transition-group selectors to create a smooth crossfade effect between the two sections.
steps.hint: Use the opacity property with transition or animation on the ::view-transition-group pseudo-elements to make them fade in and out.
steps.expectedOutcome: The two sections will smoothly crossfade when transitioning, with one fading out as the other fades in.
successCriteria: Opacity transitions are applied to the ::view-transition-group selectors to create a crossfade effect.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a crossfade effect between the sections using opacity transitions on the view-transition-group.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some opacity styling, but make sure it's applied to the ::view-transition-group selectors to create a proper crossfade effect.
steps.feedbackWrong: The crossfade effect isn't implemented correctly. Check that you're using opacity transitions on the ::view-transition-group pseudo-elements.
